<text style="bold">VERES </text>- <text style="bold">VEssel RESponse program</text> is a <text style="bold,underline">Strip Theory Program</text> which calculates wave-induced loads on and motions of mono-hulls and barges in deep to very shallow water. The Maritime Research Institute Netherlands (MARIN) and AMARCON agree to cooperate in further development of SEAWAY. MARIN<text style="bold"> </text>is an internationally recognized authority on hydrodynamics, involved in frontier breaking research programs for the maritime and offshore industries and navies.
SEAWAY is developed by Professor J.M.J. Journée at the Delft Univ. of Technology

SEAWAY is a <text style="bold,underline">Strip Theory Program</text> to calculate wave-induced loads on and motions of mono-hulls and barges in deep to very shallow water. When not accounting for interaction effects between the hulls, also catamarans can be analyzed. Work of very acknowledged hydromechanic scientists (like Ursell, Tasai, Frank, Keil, Newman, Faltinsen, Ikeda, etc.) has been used, when developing this code.
SEAWAY has extensively been verified and validated using other computer
<text style="bold">WAMIT®</text>  is the most advanced set of tools available for analyzing wave interactions with offshore platforms and other structures or vessels.

<text style="bold">WAMIT®</text>  was developed by <text style="bold">Professor Newman</text> and coworkers at <text style="bold">MIT</text> in 1987, and it has gained widespread recognition for its ability to analyze the complex structures with a high degree of accuracy and efficiency.
Over the past 20 years WAMIT has been licensed to more than 90 industrial and research organizations worldwide.

content.content: Frequency-Dependent Hydrodynamic Added Mass, Potential Damping, and Restoring Forces:   Computed using:  WAMIT, ShipX (VERES), or Octopus SEAWAY
Nonlinear Viscous Damping and Current Loads:
ITTC quadratic drag formulation/ added resistance in surge (includes current)
Nonlinear cross-flow drag in sway and yaw (includes currents)
Munk moment in yaw from potential coefficients
Higher order nonlinear damping terms in heave, roll, and pitch (manually added)
Maneuvering coefficients (manually added)
Nonlinear Frequency-Dependent Damping in Roll due to Bilge Keels and Anti-Rolling Tanks: Can be computed in ShipX (VERES) and Octopus (SEAWAY)
Frequency-Dependent Linear Viscous Damping in DOFs 1,2,6:  Manually added using exponential decaying functions for skin friction
Wave Loads:  1st-order (Froude-Krylov and diffraction) and 2nd-order wave loads (wave drift) are computed using 2D/3D potential theory
Wind Loads:  Computed using wind coefficient tables
